name: Sigma-Mixer (CDS OR-of-dhtuple ring mixer)
description: An Ergo-style equal-denomination privacy mixer whose anonymity comes from a CDS OR-of-dhtuple Σ-protocol ring proof (sigma_verify). Each ring branch is a DDH tuple (G, H, P_i, nullifier): a satisfied dhtuple proves knowledge of one x with P_j = x·G AND nullifier = x·H, so the revealed nullifier is CRYPTOGRAPHICALLY BOUND to the proven secret — closing the witness-unbound-nullifier double-spend hole that an OR-of-dlog ring leaves open. H is a nothing-up-my-sleeve BN254 base with unknown dlog w.r.t. G (try-and-increment hash-to-curve over 'sigma-mixer:nullifier-base:v1'); a flat spentNullifiers map blocks double-withdraw; the bound message (nullifier ‖ recipient) makes the payout destination a signed field (anti-front-run). This e2e is scoped as CRYPTO + LIFECYCLE plumbing: economic custody (_transferAsset in/out) is exercised only in the production app, NOT here — but the B2 double-spend is still observable at the PROOF layer (flow 4), so the e2e detects the original flaw without any value movement. Anonymity set = exactly n=4 (the ring size is public, INV-3). All proofs are REAL BN254 transcripts produced offline by scripts/gen-sigma-mixer-fixture.ts and verified through the sigma_verify opcode before check-in.

events.name: withdraw (honest)
events.description: Real CDS OR-of-dhtuple proof; hides which branch j; Nf=x_j·H is witness-bound

events.name: withdraw (replay)
events.description: Same Nf replayed after spend; has(spentNullifiers,Nf) denies it

events.name: withdraw (forged nullifier, B2)
events.description: Attacker-chosen Nf' != x_j·H; shared-z dhtuple rejects it -> sigma_verify false

events.name: withdraw (bad recipient, H2)
events.description: Tampered recipientHex; message-binding === fails -> front-run defeated

testFlows.name: B1 — drive the fill: 4 deposits flip filling -> open
testFlows.description: Create with status 'filling' and an empty ring, then process 4 deposit events against ONE fiber instance. The first three keep it 'filling' (guard B: depositCount+1 < target); the 4th flips it to 'open' (guard A: depositCount+1 == target, declared FIRST). This exercises the mutually-exclusive open-first deposit ordering — the regression the original design omitted (it pinned 'open' and never tested the flip).

testFlows.name: Honest withdraw — ring proof verifies, payout advances
testFlows.description: Create with the pinned 4-point ring (status 'open'). A real CDS OR-of-dhtuple withdrawal proves membership in the ring while hiding which branch, reveals the witness-bound nullifier, and binds the recipient into the Fiat-Shamir message. withdrawCount 0+1 < 4, so the fiber stays 'open' (the ->open variant fires).

testFlows.name: Double-spend (same Nf) — replay after spend is denied
testFlows.description: An honest withdraw records its nullifier; the IDENTICAL withdraw replayed cannot spend again because has(spentNullifiers, Nf) is now true and the `!has` clause denies it. INV-2.

testFlows.name: B2 — forged nullifier rejected at the PROOF layer
testFlows.description: The core B2 regression: a SECOND spend of the same branch under an ATTACKER-CHOSEN nullifier Nf' != x_j·H. Because H has unknown dlog w.r.t. G, the shared-z dhtuple equality cannot hold for Nf', so sigma_verify returns false and the guard denies — WITHOUT any custody/value movement, proving the e2e detects the original drain-the-ring flaw. INV-1.

testFlows.name: H2 — front-run (swapped recipient) rejected
testFlows.description: A mempool front-runner replays the proof with a DIFFERENT recipientHex. The message-binding clause (message == Nf ‖ recipient) fails, AND the strong-FS root challenge folded the original message, so sigma_verify also fails. The payout destination is effectively a signed field. INV-4.
